fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Walkway
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with tall reflective posts on both sides so it remains visible at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Trim trees and shrubs along both sides of the driveway so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Maintain vertical clearance along the full length of the driveway to allow passage of fire apparatus and ambulances.
• Clear a turnaround area near the main residence large enough for a fire engine to reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Mark or designate a flat, firm staging area near the residence where responders can park and work without blocking the driveway.
• Thin dense vegetation along the driveway to reduce the risk of fire spreading from vegetation to vehicles or structures during an emergency.
• Keep the path between the main residence and the detached structure clear so responders can move between the two buildings on foot.
• Post a property map or site diagram at the driveway entrance showing the location of the residence, detached structure, and any gates or barriers along the drive.
• If a gate is present at the driveway entrance, install a Knox Box or provide emergency responders with keypad access so entry is not delayed.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Trees; Mixed Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Terrain; Single Access Route; Long Driveway; Grass Cover; Brush Area; Limited Vegetation Separation; Tree Cluster; Adequate Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches and shrubs that are directly touching or overhanging the house and any other structures on the property.
• Thin the tree cluster visible near the structures to create open space between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or within a few feet of the structures.
• Cut grass short around the structures and along the driveway, especially in the open terrain areas where dry grass can carry fire quickly.
• Clear brush from the areas immediately surrounding the structures where brush growth is concentrated.
• Separate shrubs and small trees in mixed vegetation areas near the structures so fire cannot easily move from one plant to the next toward the house.
• Keep the full length of the driveway clear of overhanging branches so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from the brush areas closest to the structures.
• Maintain the open areas that already exist between vegetation and structures — do not allow new shrub or brush growth to fill those gaps.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate from the road, supporting access along the single entry route.
• Thin scattered trees on the sides of the driveway where branches hang low or vegetation crowds the travel lane.
• Keep grass along the driveway edges cut short for the full length of the drive.
